languages: non-English (prompting language not specified in abstract)

links.outcome: Decision accuracy and speed of students with vs without LLM access in trauma simulation
links.effect: LLM support did not enhance decision accuracy or speed; longer response times in some complex cases; teamwork median 3.5 vs 5.0 (P=.08); confidence gains larger without LLM (P=.02).
links.quote: LLM support did not enhance the decision accuracy or speed and was associated with longer response times in some complex cases.

links.outcome: Effect of non-English prompting on LLM performance
links.effect: Non-English prompting likely contributed to lower AI performance; students reported vague or overly general responses.
links.quote: The use of non-English prompting likely contributed to lower AI performance, underscoring the importance of language alignment in LLM applications.

unlisted_practices: unstructured versus structured LLM use in medical education

screen.reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating the impact of unstructured LLM assistance versus control on medical students' decision-making and teamwork in simulated trauma scenarios.
